newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gold fall overshadows commodity sector.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gold fall overshadows commodity sector.

text.p: The collapsing gold price cast a pall over the commodity sector where most prices drifted lower in relatively slow trading on Monday.

Another near $10 an ounce loss in the price of gold bullion in Europe to around 12 year lows of just under $315 an ounce, and forecasts of more losses to come, left investors shell-shocked and prompted the closure of a South African mine.
South Africa's East Rand Proprietary Mines said it would halt work at its Benoni Gold Mining Co Ltd due to the slide in the gold price.

"It's very bad news. They are calling it down to below $300 an ounce and if it does go to that there will be only three, four or maybe five mines in South Africa..." said Leon Esterhuizen, analyst at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak in Johannesburg.

The market's sell-off continued to stem from the complete loss of confidence in the yellow metal as a store of wealth following last week's news the Australian central bank had sold 167 tonnes from its reserves.
In London the price did manage a small rally late in the day to around $318.00 as investors who had made sales ahead of the collapse brought them back at a profit.
On the Chicago Board of Trade the price of wheat dropped to contract lows as active harvesting of the winter wheat crop in ideal weather conditions revealed above average yields.
The July red winter wheat futures position was trading around $3.14 a bushel, down around six cents from Thursday. (Chicago was shut Friday for Independence Day.)
Favourable weather in Brazil, the world's number one producer, was a factor behind a further downward drift in the price of coffee beans with London robusta futures dipping $38 a tonne to $1,740.
Broker GNI said Brazil's coffee regions would now be frost free through the middle of July based on latest weather forecasts.
"While there is still the possibility of a frost through to the end of August, the risks from here drop sharply," GNI said in a daily report.
